warnings: Multi-site, multi-year design: data are pooled across 5 European sites (Jokioinen, Tervuren, Giessen, Göteborg, Sutton Bonington) and 2 years (1998-1999); degrees of freedom vary by element and tissue
Factorial design with both CO2 and O3 treatments: four treatment groups exist (NF, 680, O3, 680O3); extract CO2 effect by comparing NF vs 680 only
OTC chamber effect is documented and significant (Table 6): nutrient concentrations inside OTCs differ from ambient field plots, so comparisons should be made within OTC treatments only
Two harvest times reported (intermediate = maximum leaf area; final = maturity): treat these as separate observations
Degrees of freedom (d.f.) vary by element (11 for aboveground, 11-31 for tubers) reflecting different numbers of datasets contributing to each analysis

FACE plots existed at some sites but were excluded from the common statistical analysis; all data in Tables 4 and 5 are OTC only
Some nutrient data unavailable (marked 'na') for certain site/organ combinations; nitrogen in aboveground biomass at intermediate harvest was not available
Manganese and zinc are reported in µg g-1 DM (micrograms), while macronutrients are in mg g-1 DM; check units carefully during extraction
The 550 ppm CO2 treatments (available only at Giessen and Sutton Bonington) were excluded from the pooled ANOVA; only 680 ppm vs ambient are compared
CO2 enrichment accelerated tuber development, so some concentration differences may partly reflect developmental stage rather than pure dilution

recon.treatment_definition: 680: OTC enriched with CO2 to yield 680 ml l-1 (approximately 664-708 ppm achieved across sites)
recon.potential_tc_confusion: The four-group factorial design (NF, 680, O3, 680O3) risks confusion. Do NOT treat O3 as the control for 680O3 comparison unless specifically extracting O3 effects. For CO2 effect: NF=control, 680=treatment. The paper sometimes reports 'percent change' in text which must be verified against table values.
recon.sample_size_source: Degrees of freedom are provided in Tables 4 and 5 (d.f. = 11 for aboveground at both harvests; d.f. = 11-31 for tubers depending on number of datasets). Individual plot/chamber replicates per treatment per site are not reported. The d.f. reflect pooled datasets across sites/years.
recon.factorial_structure: ["CO2 (ambient vs 680 ppm)", "O3 (ambient vs elevated)", "Site (5 levels)", "Year (1998 vs 1999)"]
recon.extraction_guidance: 1. Extract mineral CONCENTRATION data (not uptake) from Tables 4 and 5 as separate observations for each harvest time. 2. Use NF column as control and 680 column as elevated CO2 treatment. 3. Ignore O3 and 680O3 columns for CO2 effect extraction unless extracting O3 interaction. 4. No variance (SE/SD) is reported for the treatment means in Tables 4 and 5 — only ANOVA P-values. This severely limits meta-analysis utility; the paper may only be usable for direction/significance rather than effect size calculation unless you can obtain raw site-level data. 5. Macronutrients (N, P, K, Ca, Mg) are in mg g-1 DM; micronutrients (Mn, Zn, Fe) are in µg g-1 DM — record units carefully. 6. Treat intermediate harvest (Table 4) and final harvest (Table 5) as separate data points. 7. Treat aboveground biomass and tubers as separate organs. 8. d.f. values can be used to estimate approximate n: d.f.=11 implies ~12 total observations across treatments (approximately 3 per group if balanced 2×2 factorial), but this is pooled across sites. 9. The N aboveground biomass data at intermediate harvest is marked 'na' and should not be extracted. 10. Do not use Table 6 data for CO2 treatment effect extraction — it measures chamber effects only.
